scope: Apple leaf (appleleaf, Malus domestica leaves): add the wilted-leaf cyanic-compound caution of the cited specialist source. Verdict (limited_supplement, C) and confidence (C) are unchanged; no evidence record changes.

source_read.source: The Tortoise Table — Apple (Tree), Malus domestica
source_read.level: original page read (also read 2026-10-15; text unchanged)
source_read.quote: The pips/seeds from the apple contain cyanide and should be avoided.  The leaves, as they get older and wilt, produce a cyanic compound, so although your tortoise will come to no harm if he accidentally nibbles a few fallen leaves, it is wise to prevent him from doing so if possible.

comparison.note: The peach-tree entry carries the same wilted-leaf wording and data/public_assessments.json already states it in peachleaf's limits and why. appleleaf, citing the same kind of entry, did not.

update.english: The source explains that apple leaves produce a cyanic compound as they get older and wilt. It says a few fallen leaves nibbled by accident do no harm but advises preventing this where possible, so older, wilted or fallen leaves are not fed
update.reason: The cited source's own caution about older and wilted leaves was missing from the public limits. Added as written by the source: it distinguishes an accidental nibble (no harm) from leaves that are best not eaten; it is not a toxic dose and not a grade change.

not_changed: the seed/pip caution of the source is outside this leaf record's scope (limits already keep fruit and seed verdicts separate)
